subject: Clarify bundling + rounding for multi-model routing
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@olivetech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify bundling + rounding for multi-model routing

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — it was helpful to see OliveTech's mix of short transactional calls (avg ~18 tokens) and occasional long-document summarizations routed to larger models. A couple of follow-ups from our side so we can finalize the pilot terms and the proposed discount structure: 

- Billing unit question: do you expect the majority of requests to hit multiple model variants in a single logical session (e.g. short prompt routed to fast model + follow-up heavy-lift to larger model)? If yes, we need to confirm how we bucket/round across those hops.
- Minimums/rounding: for short calls we typically apply a per-request quantum (default 32-token floor) before aggregation. For your mix it might overcharge small conversational turns. Would you be open to a hybrid: 8-token quantum for requests under 128 tokens and standard 32-token quantum for others?
- Bundled discount mechanics: you asked about how bundle credits interact with rounding — specifically whether leftover fractional credits from rounding are applied to the account-level true-up. We usually amortize leftover tokens as account-level credits at invoice time, but adjustable per contract.

I attached a sanitized usage sample you shared (olivetech_usage_summary.csv) and a quick mock-up of how the invoice line items would look with the hybrid quantum (redwood_invoice_example.xlsx). Can you confirm the acceptance criteria for: (a) prepayed bundle consumption precedence vs. per-token billing; (b) whether per-call or per-conversation ceilings are more relevant for your finance team?

If it's okay, I'll loop in our billing lead (Karthik) to do the final arithmetic and propose two options you can present to procurement.

Thanks,

Jasmine Liu

From: Priya Shah <priya@olivetech.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify bundling + rounding for multi-model routing

Thanks Jasmine — confirming a few points from our side so the calculation matches procurement expectations: 

1) Multi-model routing: yes, we do a lot of quick intents that sometimes escalate to a stronger model in the same session (~22% of sessions). Billing should avoid double-charging the tiny prefix twice if it can be attributed to the later higher-capacity call.
2) Preference: procurement prefers account-level true-up credits rather than per-invoice line-by-line rounding adjustments. As long as the aggregated monthly invoice shows net credits rather than per-request granular items, that's fine.
3) For pilot simplicity, we prefer a lower floor for short requests (8-token) — if the math can stay within +/-1% of expected spend vs. raw token counts, procurement will accept it.

Also FYI: our legal team asked whether discounts can be structured against net billed tokens after rounding (i.e., discount applies to the post-rounding total). That affects how we show the discount line on the invoice.

Priya Shah

Thanks Priya, this is helpful. Quick notes from the sales/ops side before Karthik weighs in: 

- Attribution rule we propose: if a short prefix (<64 tokens) is followed by a higher-capacity call within the same 30s session, we will (by default) bill only the higher-capacity call's rounded quantum and credit the prefix's floor. This prevents double-flooring.
- Bundle precedence: prepaid bundle credits will be consumed first, then per-token billing applies. Leftover rounding deltas will accumulate as a single account-level credit shown on the final invoice (not on each line).
- Discount mechanics: discount applies to the gross billed amount after rounding and bundle consumption (so procurement's ask is feasible).

I'll let Karthik confirm the exact math + provide a sample invoice that follows the procurement preference (account-level true-up credits + discount applied post-rounding). Vanessa — can you add this to the upcoming pilot SOW? Prefer an opt-in checkbox for the hybrid quantum so we can turn it on for the pilot only.

—Ben

Hi all,

Apologies for the delayed reply — ran the numbers against the usage sample Jasmine attached. Summary below and I included two worked examples (short-session aggregation + escalate-to-large-model) — see attached mock invoice for full line breakdown.

Key points: 
1) Quantum rules implemented for the pilot: 8-token quantum for requests <= 128 tokens, 32-token quantum otherwise. We will apply the session attribution rule Ben suggested: if an 8-quantum request is immediately followed by a larger call within 30s, we retract the 8-quantum charge and only bill the larger call's quantum. This prevents per-hop double-flooring.

2) Rounding math and discount application:
- Raw tokens (sum) = 1,742,913 tokens
- Post-quantum rounding (per-request) = 1,743,040 tokens (net rounding delta +127 tokens)
- Bundle consumption (prepaid 1,500,000 tokens) -> remaining billed tokens = 243,040
- Discount (15% negotiated) applied to the billed tokens amount after rounding and bundle usage -> final charge reflects discounted post-rounding total.

3) Account-level true-up: rounding deltas (the +127 tokens) will be shown as a single "Rounding credit" line and applied against next invoice if net positive. For pilot transparency we will surface the pre- and post-rounding numbers in the invoice PDF but keep the credit aggregated at account-level as requested.

Worked example A (short conversational path):
- Req #2352: 18 tokens -> rounded to 8-quantum => 8 tokens billed initially (will be retracted if followed by escalation)
- Req #2353 (same session, within 12s): escalate to large model, 1,240 tokens -> rounded to 32-quantum -> final bill: 32 tokens for the escalated call (8-token initial floor retracted).

Worked example B (isolated short calls):
- 100 isolated requests average 18 tokens -> each rounded to 8 -> total billed = 800 tokens (instead of raw 1,800). This is why the provisioning of hybrid quantum can materially reduce small-call billing.

Next steps: 
- Jasmine: confirm OliveTech is OK with the 30s session attribution window.
- Priya: confirm procurement sign-off for discount-on-post-rounding approach.
- Vanessa: include the hybrid quantum opt-in checkbox and the account-level rounding credit line in the SOW.

Attaching: redwood_invoice_example.xlsx (with sample invoice lines) and a short note on rounding policy.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Billing & Pricing Lead | Redwood Inference
